messages:
maya: seeing a steady pile of Pending pods in eu-west-2a, all request GPUs. cluster-autoscaler logs show scale-up requests but nodegroup stays at target.
ops-bot: autoscaler event: scale-up failed: nodegroup-gpu-eu-west-2a attach ENI timeout 300s (retries hit).
maya: pods show Pending: "0/0 nodes are available: 1 Insufficient gpu." — but we do have available GPUs in other zones.
samir: can you paste `kubectl get nodes -o wide` and `kubectl get pods -A | grep Pending`?
maya: pasted quick output: ```
NAME                         STATUS   ROLES    AGE   VERSION
gpu-node-1                   NotReady  <none>  2m   v1.26.3
...
```
lina: cloud console shows several ENI attaches stuck in "attaching" to the new GPU instances. Looks like the VPC ENI quota in eu-west-2a is at 95% used.
ken: why didn't autoscaler fallback to other zones/nodegroups? our policy allows cross-zone.
samir: autoscaler code has a latch that prefers same-az nodegroups if Pod topologies demand, it retries the same group until backoff. If ENI attach stalls, retries block further scale actions for that group for 10m.
maya: ops-bot also reported a long GC on kubelet causing registration delay for some nodes. combined timing bad.
lina: immediate mitigation: 1) increase ENI quota (request in progress) 2) make autoscaler ignore unready nodes by removing the group from balancing temporarily 3) patch pod tolerations to allow bursting to cpu-only fallback pools.
ken: can we just delete the stuck attach resources to force reattach? risky but might speed things.
samir: i'll try a safer path first — set the GPU nodegroup max to +30% so cloud provider can attempt new instances in other subnets. also adding `--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false` to allow rapid provisioning? hmm.
maya: rolling plan: (1) cordon NotReady GPU nodes, (2) drain low-priority jobs to cpu-fallback, (3) bump nodegroup desired/min temporarily, (4) watch autoscaler events.
ken: commands I ran: ```bash
aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters Name=status,Values=attaching
aws autoscaling update-auto-scaling-group --auto-scaling-group-name ng-gpu-eu2a --min-size 6 --desired-capacity 8
```
deploy-bot: deploy job queued: infra/patch-autoscaler v0.9.2 -> canary-2
samir: deployed a config flip: autoscaler now ignores az-affinity for 10m for pending pods labelled `redwood/allow-cross-az=true`.
maya: immediate drop in Pending after config flip, cluster started provisioning nodes in eu-west-2b and c.
ops-bot: cloud events: ENI quota increase approved (temp bump) by provider partner.
lina: follow-up: we also saw cost spike from forced fallback to on-demand GPU instances vs spot — estimate +18% for the hour.
ken: we need a postmortem on policy: the one-group latch plus ENI fragility is a single point. maybe autoscaler should detect ENI throttling and shift groups sooner.
samir: agreed. I'll open RFC: autoscaler heuristics for network attach failures + global fallback.
maya: immediate action items: 
- samir: RFC + patch autoscaler to expose ENI failure signal (P0)
- lina: raise permanent ENI quota for eu-west-2a and enable cross-subnet attach fallback
- ken: add cost alert for on-demand GPU surge (threshold 10% hourly)
- maya: create a runbook step to manually toggle az-affinity when ENI attach rate exceeds X

maria (via message to ops channel): marking incident resolved — capacity restored, pods scheduling, watching for regressions. :white_check_mark:
